newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa to open office in Norway.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa to open office in Norway.

text.p: Swedish insurance company Trygg-Hansa AB said on Thursday it will open an office in Oslo, Norway, during the spring.

"Our aim with the new office is to take care of our customers' interests in company and industrial insurance," said Fredrik Rosencrantz, head of the business unit for large companies within Trygg-Hansa.
Initially, the office will be manned by three people from Zurich/Protector in Oslo, headed by Karl-Erik Mjones, the company said in a statement.
Trygg-Hansa was previously active in the Norwegian market through Protector Forsikring of which Trygg-Hansa owned 10 percent.
But during the autumn of 1995, Zurich bought Trygg-Hansa's stake and Trygg-Hansa then decided to set up its own operations, the company said.
